clips.q: It’s game over for the Sega Dreamcast.
We hereby announce our decision to stop production of Dreamcast as of the March term of 2001.
clips.who: **Hideki Sato**, Sega vice president, as translated by the Associated Press, January 31, 2001[^4]

clips.q: Sega remains committed to the Dreamcast format going forward.
clips.who: **Charles Bellfield**, Sega of America, eight days before the exit, quoted by the Register[^13]

clips.q: Pirates are parasites that hurt this community and will not be tolerated by Sega.
We are not going to hang around for three or four years to wait for broadband, but when it’s there, we’re ready to go.
Dreamcast was a phenomenal 18 months of pain, heartache, euphoria…
I’ve never met anybody who regretted buying a Dreamcast.
We had the content right. We had the marketing right. The product was designed right.
